name: shntool
desc: Multi-purpose tool for manipulating and analyzing WAV files
why: A swiss-army knife for WAV files that can split, analyse and inspect audio with a surprising range of tricks.

brief.what_it_is: shntool is a multi-purpose WAVE data processing and reporting utility, shipped as a set of command-line tools (shncat, shncmp, shnconv, shncue, shnfix, shngen, shnhash, shninfo, shnjoin, shnlen, shnpad, shnsplit, shnstrip, shntool, shntrim). It takes WAVE audio as input and produces processed or reported output. The homepage says it can handle any file that contains WAVE data, compressed or not, provided a format module exists for that file type. Native support covers .wav files, and other lossless formats need an external helper program.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit motivation beyond describing itself as a WAVE processing and reporting utility, with format handling separated from the core so new formats can be added. The homepage has no ChangeLog or statement of purpose beyond that.
brief.how_it_works: The core is format-agnostic, and file formats are handled through separate modules. For non-WAV formats such as FLAC, APE, WavPack, TTA or Shorten, shntool calls an external helper program, which must be installed. Some helpers have patched versions the homepage recommends for full functionality.
brief.install_notes: On Windows, copy the helper program executable into the same directory as shntool.exe, or into any directory on your PATH. On Unix, install the helper programs for the formats you need; the homepage's table lists per-format unix and win32 availability and a 'patched for' column recommending patched builds. The homepage offers a source download (216061 bytes) and a win32 download (111759 bytes) for version 3.0.10. No accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration are mentioned.
brief.standout: The format-module design lets one tool work across many lossless codecs by delegating to helper binaries, and Windows users only need to drop executables on the PATH. The page also hosts a bug list and a note that it has been run on an iPod Touch.
brief.status: Quiet. The only release listed is 3.0.10 (stable), dated 2009-03-30, and the page lists no later version. The page has a 'Known bugs' section and a contact address, but I saw no commit history or newer release. Treat it as unmaintained-looking, with no evidence of recent activity.
brief.caveats: Native support is for .wav only; other formats depend on helper programs, several of which are old (for example FLAC 1.2.1, Shorten 3.6.1) and some are 'src' only, so you may need to build them. Known bug: shntool fails to determine the correct size or length of very large files, possibly 64-bit related. Padding tiny files up to the CD-DA 4-second minimum is a feature suggestion, not an implemented feature. The homepage gives no licence information.
quotes: shntool is a multi-purpose WAVE data processing and reporting utility.
File formats are abstracted from its core, so it can process any file that contains WAVE data, compressed or not - provided there exists a format module to handle that particular file type.
Check out shntool in action on an iPod Touch!
